Scale and detail

Small patterns work best with clear profiles and a few defining traits: shell pattern, eye, tongue or major markings. Individual scales rarely need to be reproduced one by one.

Work in stitch dimensions rather than pixels alone. The same artwork may work at 120 stitches wide and lose its identity completely when reduced to 45. Color and style

For snakes, repeated markings can become a rhythm of color. Turtle shells support geometric treatment; on lizards, tail shape and toes help preserve character.

Limit colors deliberately. Every extra shade should add volume, separation or identity; if it appears in only a few stitches without changing the image, it may add work rather than quality. Rights and accuracy where relevant
